universal.description: Whether the profile represents an individual creator, founder-led brand or another single creator identity.
The outcomes the creator expects from using the Creator Brain.
Channels where the profile should support creation.
Languages and locale expectations for content.
Subjects and life areas that must remain outside the profile.
Boundary between usable public identity and private information.
Name the system should use for the creator.
How the creator presents themselves publicly.
Current professional context relevant to content.
Roles from which the creator speaks or creates.
Areas where the creator can make authoritative claims.
Relevant experiences that may support authentic stories or opinions.
Credentials, results and evidence that substantiate authority.
Current work and themes the creator wants associated with their identity.
Category or territory in which the creator wants to be understood.
Concise statement connecting creator, audience, problem and distinctive value.
Value the audience can consistently expect from the creator's content.
The creator's distinct perspective, mechanism or combination of experience.
Topics the creator owns or intends to own.
Beliefs and principles that shape the creator's point of view.
Common ideas, practices or narratives the creator explicitly rejects.
Meaningful differences from alternatives or adjacent creators.
How the creator wants the audience to describe them.
Claims the creator may make and claims that require qualification or must be avoided.
Primary audience the content is designed to help or influence.
Secondary audiences that may be served without diluting the primary audience.
Typical knowledge and problem-awareness level of the primary audience.
Important problems, pains and jobs the audience is trying to resolve.
Outcomes, identity and progress the audience wants.
Reasons the audience resists the creator's ideas, methods or offers.
Words, phrases and conceptual frames naturally used by the audience.
Incorrect assumptions the content should correct.
Change the content should help the audience achieve.
Factors that prevent the audience from trusting the creator or message.
Concise description of the recognizable creator voice.
Stable personality traits expressed through content.
Default tone and permitted contextual variations.
Formality, technicality and social register.
Pacing, paragraph density and sentence-length tendencies.
Preferred terminology, recurring words and vocabulary exclusions.
Recognizable rhetorical and structural habits worth preserving.
How the creator uses personal stories, cases and narrative progression.
Allowed humor, emotional intensity and emotional boundaries.
Expected depth, assumed knowledge and explanation behavior.
Opening patterns that fit or do not fit the creator.
Preferred content progression and ending patterns.
Language and stylistic behaviors that must never be used.
Representative content or calibrated outputs explicitly approved as on-voice.
Examples and reasons that define what is off-voice.
Outcomes content should produce for audience and creator.
Observable signals that content is serving its intended purpose.
Stable thematic pillars with clear purpose and boundaries.
Supporting topics that reinforce rather than dilute the pillars.
Recurring narratives that connect beliefs, experience and audience transformation.
Desired balance between education, opinion, proof, story and commercial content.
Formats that fit the creator's strengths and goals.
Purpose of each active channel.
Rules for using inspiration while protecting original thought and attribution.
Research, citation, recency and fact-checking expectations.
Subjects, timing and conditions under which content must not be prepared as publishable.
How ideas may be adapted without losing context, provenance or channel fit.
Named methods and frameworks the creator owns or uses.
Approved personal or professional stories with usage boundaries.
Approved cases, outcomes and proof available for content.
Developed opinions that can support creator-led content.
Questions repeatedly asked by the audience or clients.
Approved reusable diagrams, models, data and content assets.
Source types or named sources the creator trusts.
Limits on what may be claimed from available knowledge and proof.
How proactively the AI should propose angles, claims and improvements.
When the AI should ask and when it may proceed with a declared assumption.
Actions allowed without approval and decisions reserved for the user.
How missing evidence, ambiguity and disagreement must be communicated.
Expected behavior when rewriting or adapting creator material.
How corrections become proposed profile improvements.
Rules for retaining source metadata, excerpts and private information.
Actions the Creator Brain must never take or imply it has taken.
Minimum standard a deliverable must meet before presentation.
Realistic tasks used to test the profile.
Observable criteria for successful outputs across representative tasks.
Critical errors that invalidate an output.
Confirmed choices made during scenario and output calibration.
Results of representative profile tests.

commercial.activation_condition: Content supports an offer, product, service, lead action or commercial relationship.

fields.description: Current offer or offer portfolio relevant to content.
Problem each offer is designed to solve.
Credible transformation associated with the offer.
Method or mechanism through which the offer creates value.
Approved proof that may substantiate offer-related content.
How content should connect to the offer without distorting editorial value.
Permitted calls to action and their appropriate contexts.
Commercial claims and selling behaviors that must be avoided.

multi_channel.activation_condition: The creator wants the profile to support more than one channel with meaningful adaptation.

fields.description: Voice, depth and format differences required by each channel.
Elements that must remain stable across channels.
Rules for adapting an idea without merely copying its expression.

team_brand.activation_condition: Multiple people create, approve or publicly represent the same creator brand.

fields.description: People or roles with authority over the creator profile.
Required content and profile approval sequence.
Shared brand rules that override individual stylistic preferences.
Who may speak for which topics, claims and experiences.
